To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decrease of Abeta levels in the aged brain by administration of an AO directed at the Abetaregion of APP reduces protein oxidation and improves memory deficits in aged SAMP mice.
the specific protein levels of Aldo3, Coro1a, Prdx2 and Pro-2 are changed by decreasing the level of Abeta in aged brain in SAMP8 mice.

the specific protein oxidation levels of Aldo3, Coro1a and Prdx2 were significantly decreased in the aged SAMP8 mouse brain treated with AO against Abeta region compared to that of age-controlled SAMP treated with random AO.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanism of learning and memory improvement of aged SAMP8 following the administration of an Abeta antisense oligonucloetide and the possible role of Abeta reduction in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
the identification of the proteins that are oxidatively modified in aged SAMP-8 mice and the effects of Abeta reduction on these proteins.
identifying the proteins that are oxidized in brains from aged mice and that may be less oxidized in brains of aged SAMP8 treated mice following AO against the Ab region of APP administration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the decrease of Abeta levels in brains of aged accelerated mice by the antisense oligonucelotide against Abeta region of Amyloid Precursor Protein gene may contribute to the improvement of memory and learning performance of aged mice through the reduction of oxidative stress and the alteration of expression of proteins involved in energy metabolism and actin polymerization.

the administration of AO against the Abbeta region of APP in aged SAMP 8 mice reduces oxidative stress and improves learning and memory deficits by decreasing the level of Abbeta and the specific protein carbons in brain.
decreasing Abeta level in the brains of aged SAMP8 may be one of the mechanisms of restoring the learning, memory and cognitive deficits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decrease in Abeta production by antisense oligonudeotides against the Abeta-region of APP may improve the learning and memory performance in aged mice through the decrease in the oxidative stress in the brains.
the decrease of the production of Abetas may be one of the mechanisms of restoring the learning deficits in aged SAMP mice.
the decrease in Abeta level in aged brain may contribute to the mechanisms of improving memory and cognitive deficits through reduction of oxidative protein damage in aged SAMP mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found a number of proteins in brain that were less oxidized in aged mice that received AO against Abeta region of Amyloid Precursor Protein.

the reduction of the level of Abeta by antisense oligonucelotide directed at the region of APP gene that encodes Abeta in aged mice brain can reduce the oxidative stress of the brain and improve the cognitive function.
decreasing Abeta level by antisense oligonucletide may be a potential therapeutic target for Alzheimer's disease.
